paragraphs: A positive integer is a perfect square exactly when every exponent in its prime factorisation is even.

Each prime factor of a square comes from multiplying two identical factorisations. Positive divisors pair as d and n/d; only the square root pairs with itself. Therefore perfect squares have an odd number of positive divisors.

sections.heading: Understand the idea
paragraphs: The difference between consecutive squares is an odd number: (n+1)²−n²=2n+1.

sections.heading: Understand the idea
paragraphs: Scientific notation writes a nonzero number as c×10ᵉ with 1≤|c|<10 and integer e. This separates the leading digits from the scale.

objectives: Explain comparing quantities in scientific notation.

sections.heading: Understand the idea
paragraphs: To compare positive numbers in normalized scientific notation, compare exponents first and coefficients second.
